channel.title: ICU Scope
channel.description: Daily-updated ICU/critical-care literature and FOAMed, organized by organ system.

item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of pyroptosis in sepsis‑induced acute lung injury (Review).
item.description: This review explores the mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of pyroptosis in sepsis-induced acute lung injury. Pyroptosis is a critical driver of lung injury and inflammation, and its pathways can be targeted for personalized treatments. Researchers have identified biomarkers and potential inhibitors to enable more effective interventions.

item.title: Fluid and Electrolyte Management in Critically Ill Patients with Infections.
item.description: Critically ill patients with infections struggle to maintain fluid balance due to increased capillary permeability and organ dysfunction. Inadequate fluid balance can increase complications, morbidity, and mortality. Skilled nursing and advanced monitoring are essential to optimize outcomes.

item.title: Erratum: AASLD Practice Guidance on Acute-on-chronic liver failure and the management of critically ill patients with cirrhosis.
Rocuronium dose and first-attempt intubation success in the critically ill: secondary analysis of two multicenter trials.
item.description: Researchers analyzed data from 2 large studies to see if a higher dose of rocuronium helped patients get intubated on the first try in the ICU. They found that a higher dose of rocuronium was associated with a slightly higher chance of successful intubation on the first attempt, especially in the ICU. This difference was not seen in emergency department intubations.

item.title: Inflammatory Phenotypes In Severe Pneumonia: Clinical Evidence To Mouse Models For Precision Therapeutics.
item.description: Researchers identified two inflammatory phenotypes in patients with severe pneumonia: a hyperinflammatory phenotype with worse outcomes and a hypoinflammatory phenotype with better outcomes. They also developed a mouse model that mimics these phenotypes and found that anti-inflammatory interventions only benefited the more inflamed mice. This study provides a framework for developing targeted therapies for critical illness.

item.title: Daptomycin vs. Vancomycin for the Treatment of Methicillin Resistant S. Aureus Bacteremia
item.description: This study compares the effectiveness of daptomycin and vancomycin in treating MRSA bloodstream infections. The study is a randomized controlled trial that will directly compare these two commonly used therapies. No results are reported.

item.title: Optimization of Beta-lactam Dosing in Critically Ill Patients With Cystatin C (OPTIMIZE-GNI)
item.description: This study compares the accuracy of two methods (Cystatin C and eGFR equations) for estimating kidney function in critically ill patients with suspected or documented AMR Gram-negative infections. The study aims to optimize beta-lactam dosing in these patients. The study will involve up to 200 adult patients in an ICU.

item.title: JUST BREATHE, Breathing Life Into Innovative Therapies for ARDS (Master Record)
item.description: This study is a Phase 2 trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of host-directed therapeutics in adults with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS). The trial uses a platform trial design and will randomize participants to receive either a placebo or an active treatment. The study aims to assess the safety and efficacy of these innovative therapies.

item.title: JUST BREATHE, Breathing Life Into Innovative Therapies for ARDS- Cohort C: Bevacizumab
item.description: This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of bevacizumab in hospitalized adults with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) using a platform trial design. Participants are randomized to receive either a placebo or bevacizumab. The study is a Phase 2 multicenter, randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial.

item.title: Peripheral Perfusion Index Trajectory to Predict 28-Day Mortality in Patients With Sepsis in the Intensive Care Unit
item.description: Researchers investigated whether the trajectory of peripheral perfusion index can predict 28-day mortality in ICU patients with sepsis. They found that the perfusion index trajectory may be linked to worse outcomes in these patients. The study aimed to identify a potential biomarker for sepsis severity.

item.title: JUST BREATHE, Breathing Life Into Innovative Therapies for ARDS- Cohort A: Vilobelimab
item.description: This study is evaluating the safety and efficacy of vilobelimab in hospitalized adults with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) using a platform trial design. Participants are being randomized to receive either a placebo or vilobelimab. The study aims to assess the benefits of host-directed therapeutics in ARDS patients.

item.title: Mobile-based Obstetric Monitoring for Pregnancies Complicated by Hypertension and/or Diabetes (MOM-HD)
item.description: The study discusses the potential of mobile-based obstetric monitoring for pregnancies complicated by hypertension and/or diabetes. Effective management of these conditions relies on regular monitoring of blood pressure and blood glucose. Telemonitoring is proposed as a cost-effective alternative.

item.title: Oxygen Extraction-guided Transfusion
item.description: This study evaluated the use of oxygen extraction ratio (O2ER) to guide red blood cells transfusion (RBCT) in critically ill patients. The previous study showed that O2ER can help identify the correct timing for RBCT, which may affect 90-day mortality. The current study aimed to further investigate this relationship.

item.title: JUST BREATHE, Breathing Life Into Innovative Therapies for ARDS- Cohort B: Paridiprubart
item.description: This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of paridiprubart in hospitalized adults with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) using a platform trial design.

item.title: Housing Transitions QUERI
item.description: The VA Grant and Per Diem case management aftercare program provides six months of case management for homeless-experienced Veterans undergoing housing transitions. A Partnered Implementation Initiative proposes to implement and evaluate Critical Time Intervention in 32 case management sites. This intervention aims to support housing transitions.

item.title: Predictive Validity of the Chelsea Critical Care Physical Assessment Tool (CPAx) for Regaining Autonomy Three Months After ICU Discharge
item.description: This study evaluated the relationship between the CPAx score at ICU discharge and the 6MWT distance 3 months later in patients who experienced prolonged mechanical ventilation and had signs of malnutrition, muscular weakness, or post-traumatic stress symptoms.

item.title: Effect of Structured Education for Family Members of Intensive Care Patients Undergoing Tracheostomy
item.description: This study evaluated the effect of structured education for family members of ICU patients undergoing tracheostomy on their anxiety, well-being, and satisfaction with care. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention or control group. The study aimed to assess the impact of this education on family members' emotional and psychological state.

item.title: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of AZD4144in Participants With Sepsis-associated Acute Kidney Injury.
item.description: This study is investigating the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of AZD4144 in patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either AZD4144 or a placebo. The study aims to enroll adults aged 18 to 80 years diagnosed with sepsis due to a bacterial infection.

item.title: Induced Blood-Stage Malaria in Healthy Malaria-Naive Adults to Assess the Safety and Infectivity of Plasmodium Vivax Challenge Agent and Evaluate Transmission in Mosquito Feeding Assays
item.description: Researchers induced blood-stage malaria in healthy adults to study malaria development, immune response, and transmission to mosquitoes. The study aimed to understand how malaria progresses in people and how it spreads to mosquitoes. Participants were healthy individuals aged 18-54 from the Washington DC area.

item.title: Blunt cerebrovascular injury
item.description: This article discusses the management of blunt cerebrovascular injury, including expanded Denver screening, CTA diagnosis, Biffl grading, antithrombotic treatment, and follow-up.

item.title: Anti-CD14 Treatment With IC14 in Hospitalized ARDS Patients
item.description: Patients with ARDS were given a treatment targeting CD14 or a placebo. The treatment's effect on oxygen levels was measured over 28 days. The goal was to see if the treatment improved oxygenation by day 4.

item.title: Phase 2b Study to Investigate the Safety and Efficacy of TIN816 in Sepsis-associated Acute Kidney Injury (CLEAR-AKI)
item.description: This Phase 2b study investigated the safety and efficacy of TIN816 in patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). Three different single doses of TIN816 were evaluated in hospitalized adult participants in an intensive care setting. The study aimed to characterize the dose-response relationship.

item.title: Microbiome and Enteric Signatures in Sepsis-associated Hepatorenal Injury
item.description: Researchers investigated the relationship between gut microbiome and enteric signatures in patients with sepsis-associated hepatorenal injury. They found that altered gut microbial diversity and microbial metabolites may contribute to hepato-renal injury during sepsis. However, prospective longitudinal evidence in patients with sepsis-associated liver injury and acute kidney injury remains limited.

item.title: Ultrasound vs. Nasofibroscopy for Evaluating Dysphagia After Extubation in the ICU
item.description: This observational study compared the diagnostic performance of bedside cervical ultrasonography to nasofibroscopy (FEES) for detecting post-extubation dysphagia in critically ill adult patients. The study aimed to evaluate the degree of diagnostic concordance between the two methods. No significant results were reported.

item.title: SEPSIS EARLY WARNING: NEWS2 VS MACHINE LEARNING
item.description: This study compared the early warning performance of a NEWS2-based clinical decision support system (KDS) to a machine learning model in predicting sepsis diagnosis. The NEWS2-based KDS provided an alert 4.5 hours before sepsis diagnosis, on average. The machine learning model was externally validated on 2000 patients.

item.title: Fecal Lactate and Resuscitation Outcomes in Critical Illness
item.description: This study investigated the use of fecal lactate as an early biomarker of tissue hypoperfusion in critically ill patients. Fecal lactate levels were measured within the first 12-24 hours to predict poor response to resuscitation at 24 hours. The study found that fecal lactate levels were associated with resuscitation outcomes.

item.title: Long-Term Outcomes and Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: Investigating the Associations Between Metabolic Signatures and Physical Functioning in Critically Ill Patients
item.description: Researchers studied metabolic signatures in young, healthy ICU patients to understand why some experience poor functional recovery despite being physically fit. They found that non-modifiable factors like age and pre-existing disease only explain part of the variation in recovery. The study aims to identify other underlying factors contributing to long-term recovery.

item.title: Ultrasound Detection of Body Composition in Critical Care
item.description: Researchers used ultrasound to measure body composition in critically ill patients, finding it a valuable and accessible tool.

item.title: Risk Factors for Adverse Outcomes in Sepsis
item.description: Researchers studied 567 critically ill patients to identify early signs of sepsis. They found that a specific protein, matrix metalloproteinase-3, was associated with sepsis. This protein was present at admission and may help predict sepsis outcomes.

item.title: Role of the Kallikrein-kinin System in Septic Cardiomyopathy
item.description: Researchers studied the kallikrein-kinin system in septic cardiomyopathy to see if certain molecules are differently expressed and how they are regulated.

item.title: Fast Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing for Gram Negative Bacteremia Trial
item.description: This study compared standard antibiotic testing to a faster testing method for patients with Gram-negative bacteria in their blood. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either standard testing or faster testing, in addition to standard testing. The faster testing method did not improve clinical outcomes.

item.title: Wireless MicroPremVitals Button Sensor in the NICU
item.description: Researchers developed a small, wireless sensor to monitor vital signs in extremely preterm babies, including heart rate, oxygen levels, and body temperature.

item.title: Adrenal Function in Critical Illness
item.description: This study looked at how often adrenal insufficiency happens in critically ill patients and why it's a problem. They found that it occurs in up to 77% of cases, but there's no standard way to diagnose it. Researchers need to figure out how to identify and treat adrenal insufficiency.

item.title: Real-time Evaluation and Continuous Observation of Vital Signs for Enhanced Recovery: a Study for the Early Identification of Complications in the Surgical Ward Following Surgery in Patients Not Eligible for Intensive Care Admission.
item.description: This study used wearable devices to monitor vital signs in surgical patients not eligible for ICU admission, aiming to detect postoperative complications earlier than standard hospital monitoring. The devices, Portrait Mobile, were tested in patients after major urologic surgery. The study observed the devices' ability to detect early signs of complications.

item.title: Electrical Impedance Tomography-Guided Identification of the Optimal Lateral Position in Postoperative ARDS
item.description: This study used a new imaging technique to find the best position for patients with lung problems after surgery. They compared lying on the left or right side versus lying flat, and found that one position worked better than the others. The best position helped improve how well oxygen was delivered to the lungs.

item.title: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) Score and Organ Dysfunction in Septic Shock Patients
item.description: This study investigated the relationship between Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) score and organ dysfunction in septic shock patients. DIC is a common condition in patients with sepsis and septic shock, and its coexistence with septic shock increases mortality and morbidity. The study aimed to understand the impact of DIC on organ dysfunction in septic shock patients.

item.title: Postinsertion care practices for nontunnelled dialysis catheters in intensive care: A cross-sectional survey.
item.description: Australian critical care nurses were surveyed about their postinsertion care practices for non-tunnelled dialysis catheters. The survey found variability in practices, with common methods including inspecting insertion sites, using chlorhexidine gluconate-impregnated dressings, and securing catheters with sutures. Troubleshooting methods also varied.

item.title: Risk Factors and Development of a Clinical Prediction Model for Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Bacteremia: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description: Researchers analyzed 895 patients with Enterobacterales bacteremia to identify risk factors for carbapenem resistance and predictors of mortality. They found that ICU admission, prolonged hospitalization, and prior carbapenem exposure increased the risk of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) bacteremia. Patients with CRE bacteremia had higher 28-day mortality rates compared to those with susceptible bacteria.

item.title: Plasma versus Whole Blood Multiplex Droplet Digital PCR for Pathogen Detection in ICU Patients with Clinically Suspected Sepsis: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
item.description: Researchers compared plasma and whole-blood tests for detecting pathogens in ICU patients with suspected sepsis. Both tests found more pathogens than traditional blood culture, but whole-blood tests detected more Candida infections. The results suggest both tests can complement blood culture.

item.title: Fosfomycin as an adjunctive agent against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii: an updated narrative review.
item.description: This study reviewed 48 studies on using fosfomycin to treat carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii infections. Fosfomycin may help when combined with other antibiotics, especially sulbactam, imipenem, and colistin. However, its independent contribution to treatment outcomes is unclear.

item.title: The Self-Perceived Role 2 Preparedness of Family Medicine Physicians.
item.description: This study surveyed 298 Family Medicine physicians about their preparedness to deliver Role 2 care in combat settings. Most had little experience and felt unprepared, but those with more experience and training felt more confident. Factors associated with perceived preparedness included career Role 2 experience, recent training, and caring for critically ill patients.

item.title: A Field Guide to Evidence Based Medicine Podcast – Episode 1
item.description: This podcast is the first episode of a new series on evidence-based medicine in emergency medicine, hosted by Rory and Jerry Hoffman.

item.title: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting subsyndromal delirium in critically ill patients in the emergency department.
item.description: Researchers developed a tool to predict the risk of subsyndromal delirium in critically ill patients in the emergency department, using six easily available clinical variables. The tool showed excellent accuracy and can help identify patients at risk early on. This can lead to targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes.

item.title: EMCrit 430 – Questions and Answers (Members Q&A Episode 004) with Sara Crager
item.description: Dr. Sarah Crager discusses bedside shock management, moving beyond blood pressure targets to a dynamic approach. They address clinical dilemmas, including lactated Ringer's in lactic acidosis and albumin and diuretics in edematous patients. A real-world approach to fluid management is explored.

item.title: Standard-dose unfractionated heparin versus low-dose unfractionated heparin and low-molecular-weight heparin in extracorporeal life support (RATE): an open-label, randomised, non-inferiority trial.
item.description: BACKGROUND: In patients receiving extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), standard practice is full-dose intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) targeting an activated partial thromboplastin time of 2·0-2·5 times baseline to reduce thrombotic risk. This approach can increase bleeding without further reducing thrombosis compared with low-dose UFH. item.title: LOGICAL – Conservative Oxygen after Cardiac Arrest
item.description: This study investigated the effect of limiting oxygen exposure on unresponsive patients after cardiac arrest. The results showed that conservative oxygen therapy did not increase the likelihood of survival. The study included 1200 patients.

item.title: Emergency Evidence Updates – June 2026
item.description: This is a monthly update of critical care literature, summarizing recent studies and findings.

item.title: Critical Care Evidence Updates – June 2026
item.description: This article provides a monthly update on recent critical care literature, highlighting new studies and findings.

item.title: Tooth brushing versus routine oral care impact on ventilator-associated pneumonia in PICU: a clinical trial.
item.description: OBJECTIVES: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a frequent and serious infection among mechanically ventilated children in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs), with oral colonization playing a key role in its pathogenesis. Effective oral hygiene measures are therefore crucial to reduce VAP incidence and improve clinical outcomes. This study aimed to compare the incidence of VAP in PICU patients receiving routine oral care versus toothbrushing with chlorhexidine, and to evaluate the impac

item.title: Association between energy adequacy and clinical outcomes in septic ICU patients stratified by modified NUTRIC score.
item.description: This study investigated the effect of early calorie delivery in critically ill patients with sepsis. It found that receiving at least 50% of estimated calorie needs within the first 5 days did not improve 28-day ICU survival. The study also identified independent predictors of mortality, including continuous renal replacement therapy and mechanical ventilation duration.

item.title: Early Identification of Recovery Potential After Acute Brain Injury Using Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy.
item.description: Researchers used a non-invasive brain imaging technique called functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to predict recovery in 33 patients with acute brain injury. The fNIRS-based model accurately predicted 6-month outcomes in 81.3% of patients, outperforming clinical models. The model also predicted recovery of behavioral responsiveness in 78.5% of patients.

item.title: Weight-adjusted fluid balance and its impact on days alive without life support in critical illness - an observational cohort study.
item.description: This study of 17,956 ICU patients found that a positive fluid balance of +7% or higher and a negative fluid balance of -4% or lower were associated with fewer days alive without life support. These thresholds were linked to worse outcomes, including increased mortality, need for organ support, and delirium. The study suggests that fluid balance is a crucial factor in ICU care.

item.title: Weight-adjusted fluid balance and its impact on days alive without life support in critical illness - an observational cohort study.
item.description: This study of 17,956 ICU patients found that a positive fluid balance of +7% or higher and a negative fluid balance of -4% or lower were associated with fewer days alive without life support. These thresholds were linked to worse outcomes, including increased mortality, need for organ support, and delirium. The study suggests that fluid balance is a crucial factor in ICU care.

item.title: Development of a population-level frfailty index using Quebec administrative data: a Canadian retrospective study.
item.description: Researchers developed a 30-item frailty index using Quebec administrative data to identify frail ICU patients. They found that frail patients were older, more likely to have dialysis on admission, and had a higher risk of in-hospital mortality. The index showed a strong correlation between frailty and mortality.

item.title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Continuous Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury in Critically Ill Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
item.description: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict acute kidney injury in ICU patients with atrial fibrillation, using data from 19,347 patients. The model, which combines electronic health record data, achieved high accuracy in predicting AKI risk. Clinicians can use this model to inform patient management decisions.

item.title: Glycemic Ratio Is a Superior Predictor of Mortality Compared With Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio in Critically Ill Patients.
item.description: This study compared two ways to predict mortality in critically ill patients: using a single blood glucose measurement at admission, and using a ratio of mean ICU blood glucose to estimated preadmission blood glucose. The study found that the ratio method was a better predictor of mortality. The best outcome was associated with a mean ICU blood glucose level that was 80-100% of the patient's preadmission level.

item.title: A Study in Priors
item.description: Researchers found that nearly half of positive medical trial results cannot be replicated, highlighting issues with trust in medical literature.
